entry_checks.binary_and_feature: A separate [[bin]] chonkstep-darwin-desktop requires native-managed-spawn. run() refuses unless built with cfg!(panic="unwind") and for aarch64 macOS with that feature (desktop_entry.rs ~221-229). Host builds never open native devices (host test host_never_opens_native_devices).
entry_checks.cli: Exact positional order with 17 or 19 args: --run, then --socket/--records/--session/--terminal/--seconds/--font-regular/--font-bold/--input pdhid, then an optional --startup-terminals 1|2. Seconds must be canonical decimal in 11-180. Paths must be absolute, at most 900 bytes, with no NUL, '.' or '..'. The socket is at most 100 bytes (resolves my X3 at the entry). The session must be lowercase hex48.
entry_checks.startup_order: Records PrivateDirectory, then session-result.txt (exclusive 0600), then a private 0700 socket parent, then the terminal executable (regular, non-empty, at most 64 MiB, executable bit, O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC), then the socket and .lock freshness check, then explicit fonts, then manager and launcher with a durable journal. Only after all of that: ListeningSocket bind, Display, INT/TERM/HUP stop-flag handlers, NativeHid::open, Pdgop::open, Server with packaged fonts, the Both seat, the standalone Shell, manager adoption and the optional startup queue. Errors before the coordinator cannot have spawned an app: startup terminals only queue typed requests, which launch inside frames.
entry_checks.fonts: FontState::from_packaged_fonts loads exactly the two explicit files (non-empty, at most 8 MiB each) into a private fontdb. It requires DejaVu Sans faces at Normal 400 and Bold 700 with no weight or style substitution and a glyph for every printable ASCII character. It does not scan the system font database. The lazy 'modern' and System 7 fallbacks use compiled-in assets (include_bytes!), not the filesystem. The generic FontState::new path is unchanged.
entry_checks.coordinator: session_entry::drive loops on stop flag, then deadline, then catch_unwind(frame), then an 8 ms pause. A frame Err or panic is recorded and the UI is never resumed. Then exactly one begin_shutdown, a cleanup poll capped at 10 s, and seal. successful() requires no frame error, cleanup Complete and no seal error. Deadline and signal are normal stops. Each frame does bounded admission work (at most 4 accepts) before dispatch, input, repaint and flush.
entry_checks.cleanup_isolation: begin_desktop_shutdown only sets closing and the manager's begin_shutdown. poll_desktop_shutdown only calls applications.poll() (status drain, the single owned waitpid, signals, journal). Neither touches the Shell, WM, PopupHost, Wayland dispatch, input or framebuffer. N1 root cause fixed: 001's service, key and pointer seams used self.desktop.take(), so a panic would drop the DesktopSession and its owned applications during unwind. 002 uses as_mut(), so the owner survives. Host test actual_popup_assertion_cannot_drop_the_desktop_owner triggers a real PopupHost assertion and shows the same audit object retained, has_failures true, and shutdown reaching Complete without touching popup state.
entry_checks.seal: Writes the CHONKDESKTOP/1 summary (elapsed, cleanup, deadline, frame_error, manager_failed) plus the manager audit snapshot to session-result.txt, then fsyncs. A retained manager failure becomes a seal error, so exit is 1. The binary prints the error and exits 1 on any unsuccessful outcome.
entry_checks.teardown_order: After drive: drop the listener, display, server (the manager has no Drop reaper, by design), input, then presenter. If cleanup was Incomplete, dropping the display disconnects any surviving app, and the frozen app's own Wayland-disconnect path cleans up its PTY.
entry_checks.startup_terminals: Default 0. With 1 or 2, run_explicit_startup_terminal checks bridge admission and calls the same typed Action::SpawnTerminal path with RequestSource::ExplicitStartup, recorded in journal and snapshot. There are no synthetic keys and no direct spawn. The count is at most MAX_APPLICATIONS (2), and it runs once per session (a host test proves the shared queue order Input, Input, ExplicitStartup, ExplicitStartup with no fake child).
entry_checks.profile_delta: The standalone theme keeps only the Close titlebar button, filtering frame hitboxes as well as menus, so no minimize/restore UI exists. The generic theme is untouched. Server::new keeps its generic FontState::new for the unchanged main; the desktop entry uses new_with_fonts.

notes.E1_signal_defaults: run() installs handlers only for INT, TERM and HUP. wayland-backend 0.3.17 sets SO_NOSIGPIPE on each client socket on macOS (src/rs/socket.rs:104-108, result ignored), and XNU honors SOF_NOSIGPIPE (uipc_syscalls.c:1389-1391), so client disconnects should not raise SIGPIPE. Setting SIGPIPE to SIG_IGN explicitly would back that up, and SIGCHLD should be set to SIG_DFL so an inherited SIG_IGN or auto-reap can never become 'ownership lost'. Both currently fail closed; neither can fake success.
notes.E2_cleanup_window_margin: The manager's worst case is TERM, 5 s, KILL, then a 3 s reap deadline, plus up to 2 s waiting for status EOF after a reap. That can reach about 10 s, equal to the coordinator's 10 s cap. Both sides then report Incomplete, so they agree, but the packet's outer budget must reserve the session's seconds + 10 s + seal + startup on top of the roughly 78 s bootstrap, inside the controller's hard bound.
notes.E3_unprocessed_startup_requests: If the session stops before the first frame services the queue, explicit startup requests never reach the manager, and the snapshot does not record them as unprocessed. Root's per-app gates should treat a requested but absent startup launch as failed, not as clean.
notes.E4_executable_toctou: The terminal executable is checked through an open descriptor, but the C shim later executes it by path. A replacement between check and exec is not excluded; package immutability is root's artifact binding (F1-style), not something this source can enforce.
notes.E5_manager_panic_window: catch_unwind covers the whole frame, including launcher.request. A panic inside manager code between a successful spawn and inserting the Application (for example in audit.spawn) would lose the PID. I saw no reachable panic there (the only expect is the pid>0 Status::new, which is checked first), but it is outside the claimed coverage.
